The '''DecipherCon website''' was the set of pages [[Decipher]] ran on [[Decipher.com|decipher.com]] for its company conventions. Each convention had its own site: [[DecipherCon 1999]] under <code>/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/</code>, [[DecipherCon 2000]] under <code>/deciphercon/2000/</code>, and [[DecipherCon 2002]] under <code>/deciphercon/2002/</code>. The sites took registrations before each convention, posted schedules, results, reports, photos and audio during it, and stayed online afterward as an archive of the coverage.<ref name="idx99">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/index.html DecipherCon 1999], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991128065643/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/index.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="idx00">[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/index.html DecipherCon 2000], Decipher (2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001116205400/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/index.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="idx02">[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/index.html DecipherCon 2002], Decipher (2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020604033707/http://decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> There was no 2001 site, because Decipher cancelled that year's convention (see [[2001 Decipher World Championship]]).

[[File:DecipherCon 2000 site side.jpg|thumb|DecipherCon 2000 site, 2000.]]

== DecipherCon 1999 ==

The 1999 site sat inside the ''DECIPHER Calendar'' section of decipher.com. [[DecipherCon 1999 website]] lists its sections and surviving pages one by one. Its home page opened "Welcome to DecipherCon 1999!" and, after the convention, told readers "DecipherCon is over. We've kept the best of our coverage for all of you!"<ref name="idx99" />

=== Before the convention ===

The registration page offered pre-registration until 31 October 1999. Pre-registered players got 50% off convention passes ($10) and a free foil Sebulba card for [[Young Jedi]].<ref name="reg99">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/register.html DecipherCon 1999: Registration], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991128100221/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/register.html Internet Archive]</ref> A prizes page listed uncut sheets from all of Decipher's card sets, original art from the art department, Japanese [[Star Wars CCG]] product and guest spots on [[Radio Free Decipher]].<ref name="prizes99">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/prizes.html DecipherCon 1999: Prizes], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991128083925/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/prizes.html Internet Archive]</ref> Other pages took pre-registration for Thursday's Wild Card tournaments and carried an event survey.<ref name="wild99">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/wildcardreg.html DecipherCon 1999: Wild Card registration], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000127190209/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/wildcardreg.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="survey99">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/survey.html DecipherCon 1999: Event survey], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000122152643/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/survey.html Internet Archive]</ref>

=== Coverage ===

After the convention the home page linked these sections:<ref name="idx99" />
* '''Notes from Lalumiere''': daily wrap-ups by [[Francis Lalumiere|Francis K. Lalumiere]], Thursday 11 November to Sunday 14 November.
* '''Vote for the champ''': a contest to pick the World Championship winners. The results page counted "more than 900 votes" for Star Wars CCG.<ref name="vote99">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/vote.html DecipherCon 1999: Vote for the champ], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000120055420/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/vote.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''Decks''': the World Championship decks.<ref name="decks99">[http://www1.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/decks/index.html DecipherCon 1999: World Championship decks], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000128052049/http://www1.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/decks/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''Audio feeds''': RealAudio from Radio Free DecipherCon (see below).
* '''Event reports''': a Report Board that was "read only". Decipher's Contributing Writers could post to it; readers could not reply.<ref name="mb99">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/messageboards/index.html DecipherCon 1999: Message boards], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000122091233/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/messageboards/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''Photos''': the full photo album (see [[DecipherCon 1999 photographs]]).<ref name="ph99">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/photos/index.html DecipherCon 1999: Photos], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000122111458/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/photos/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''Event schedule & results''': every event by day, with prize information and score pages.<ref name="events99">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events.html DecipherCon 1999: Event schedule & results], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000122042301/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''Special guests''': guests including [[Shannon Baksa]], [[Aron Eisenberg]] and [[Jeremy Bulloch]].<ref name="guests99">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/specialguests/index.html DecipherCon 1999: Special guests], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000122135443/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/specialguests/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''World Championship pages''' for Star Wars CCG, [[Star Trek CCG]] and Young Jedi, with finalists and ratings. The Star Wars page announced that [[Gary Carman]] was World Champion.<ref name="sw99">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/swworldchamp/index.html Star Wars CCG World Championship], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991128144348/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/swworldchamp/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> See [[1999 Decipher World Championship]].

=== Radio Free DecipherCon ===

The audio feeds page introduced [[Ryan Morris]] and [[Mark Tuttle]] as "the voice and tech behind Radio Free DecipherCon". It highlighted a "Meet the Champ" interview by Tuttle for each game and archived the rest by day. Listeners needed the RealAudio plug-in.<ref name="af99">[http://www1.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/index.html DecipherCon 1999: Audio feeds], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000128031222/http://www1.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> The day pages listed each clip with its time and length:
* Thursday, including [[Evan Lorentz]].<ref name="afthu">[http://www1.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/THU/index.html DecipherCon 1999: Audio feeds, Thursday], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010217093703/http://www1.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/THU/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* Friday, including a 12-minute interview with Jeremy Bulloch.<ref name="affri">[http://www1.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/FRI/index.html DecipherCon 1999: Audio feeds, Friday], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010217084830/http://www1.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/FRI/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* Saturday, with play-by-play of the finals games and interviews.<ref name="afsat">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/SAT/index.html DecipherCon 1999: Audio feeds, Saturday], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000313011020/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/SAT/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* Sunday, ending with closing comments.<ref name="afsun">[http://www1.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/SUN/index.html DecipherCon 1999: Audio feeds, Sunday], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010217090821/http://www1.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/SUN/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>

Each clip was a small <code>.ram</code> pointer file that told RealPlayer to stream a <code>.ra</code> file from Decipher's server.<ref name="ram99">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/FRI/audiofiles/rfd_99_11_12_1020.ram rfd_99_11_12_1020.ram], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010613151850/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/FRI/audiofiles/rfd_99_11_12_1020.ram Internet Archive]</ref>

=== Later years ===

The 1999 home page was still online in December 2002.<ref name="idx99-2002">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/index.html DecipherCon 1999], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20021202134155/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> By 18 January 2003 the address showed Decipher's "File not available" page.<ref name="gone99">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/ DecipherCon 1999 (File not available)], Decipher (2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030118090221/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/ Internet Archive]</ref>

== DecipherCon 2000 ==

The 2000 site moved to its own address, <code>/deciphercon/2000/</code>. After the convention its home page called the event "the Whole Shebang!" and invited readers to "Compare it to DecipherCon '99!"<ref name="idx00" /> Its sections were:
* '''Finals''': streaming video of the complete World Championship final for each game (see below).<ref name="fin00">[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/finals/index.html Championship Finals Videos], Decipher (2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001109002100/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/finals/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''Message boards''': game commentary and player comments.<ref name="idx00" />
* '''Zoom In''': the best writing from the message boards, by Lalumiere and the contributing writers [[Marcus Sheppard]], [[John Kaufeld]] and [[Jean-Luc Simard]].<ref name="rep00">[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/reports/index.html Zoom In], Decipher (2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001019084244/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/reports/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''Special guests''': [[Michonne Bourriague]] (Aurra Sing) and Shannon Baksa (Mara Jade).<ref name="idx00" />
* '''Players''': the 38 finalists from each Day One tournament, the semifinalists and the Day Two champions.<ref name="pl00">[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/players/ DecipherCon 2000: Players], Decipher (2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010124065400/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/players/ Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''Schedule''': more than 60 tournaments, with print-quality PDF schedules by game.<ref name="sched00">[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/schedule/ DecipherCon 2000 schedule], Decipher (2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20061009205800/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/schedule/ Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''Seminars''': "Straight talk from Decipher's game designers", including a [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]] question-and-answer session with [[Tom Lischke]] and [[Chuck Kallenbach]], and a Star Trek CCG design-a-card workshop with [[Tim Ellington]] and [[Bill Martinson]].<ref name="sem00">[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/seminars/ DecipherCon 2000 seminars], Decipher (2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060926140722/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/seminars/ Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''Sound Bytes''': more than 20 RealAudio interviews, dated 5 to 8 October 2000. Speakers included Mark Tuttle, Evan Lorentz, [[Justin Pakes]], Chuck Kallenbach, Shannon Baksa, Michonne Bourriague, [[Kendrick Summers]], [[Dean Irwin]], [[Matt Sokol]], [[Yannick Lapointe]] and Bill Martinson. The home page said Tuttle called Bourriague's interview "the best."<ref name="sb00">[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/soundbytes/index.html DecipherCon 2000: Sound Bytes], Decipher (2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001026143544/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/soundbytes/index.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="idx00" />
* '''Video clips''': 22 short movies dated 5, 8 and 16 October 2000, from 463 KB to 18.5 MB.<ref name="vc00">[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/videoclips/index.html DecipherCon 2000: Video clips], Decipher (2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20011118102040/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/videoclips/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>

=== Finals video ===

The finals page said: "For the first time ever, you can watch the Championship Final for your favorite Decipher game just as those at DecipherCon did." Each final came in a 20 kb or an 80 kb RealVideo version; the 80 kb version was meant for DSL, T1, cable or faster connections. The page posted the championship decks beside each video.<ref name="fin00" />
* '''Star Wars CCG''': two games between Matt Sokol and Yannick Lapointe.
* '''Star Trek CCG''': one game, with [[Brian Sykes]] as runner-up.
* '''Young Jedi''': two games, with [[Philippe Parise]] as runner-up.

Full results are on [[2000 Decipher World Championship]].

== DecipherCon 2002 ==

The 2002 site announced the convention for 31 October to 3 November 2002 at the Chesapeake Conference Center in Chesapeake, Virginia. It promised World Championships for [[The Lord of the Rings Trading Card Game]], Star Trek CCG, Star Wars CCG, Young Jedi and the Jedi Knights Trading Card Game. It called itself "your gateway to all DecipherCon 2002 information". Early sections covered general information, travel, accommodations and the championship circuit.<ref name="idx02" />

During the convention the site added a message board, ''The Daily News'' and a photo gallery. The Daily News covered the opening ceremonies, seminars, special-format tournaments, role-playing games, the Halloween party and the awards. It sent World Championship readers to DGMA.com and a read-only World Championships message board.<ref name="rep02">[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/reports/index.html The Daily News], Decipher (2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20021103024834/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/reports/index.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="ph02">[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/photos/index.html Sights of DecipherCon: Photo gallery], Decipher (2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20021102104948/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/photos/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== On Radio Free Decipher ==

[[Radio Free Decipher]], Decipher's weekly RealAudio show, talked about each convention before and after it. Its archive pages list these broadcasts about DecipherCon:<ref name="rfd-list99b">[http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/index1998-99.html RFD Archives 1998-1999 – Broadcasts 1-30], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20081207011923/http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/index1998-99.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="rfd-list00b">[http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/index2000.html RFD Archives 2000], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20081207022655/http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/index2000.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="rfd-list01">[http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/index2001.html RFD Archives 2001], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20081207022700/http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/index2001.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="rfd-list02">[http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/index2002.html RFD Archives 2002], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20081207022721/http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/index2002.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="rfd-list03b">[http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/index2003.html RFD Archives 2003], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20081207022726/http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/index2003.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* 1999: Broadcasts 24 (3 September), 26 (27 September) and 27 (8 October), and a special, ''The Sounds of DecipherCon '99''.
* 2000: Broadcast 37 (9 June), with DecipherCon news; Broadcast 38 (16 June), with [[Gary Carman]] and a DecipherCon recap; and Broadcasts 50 to 53 (15 September to 13 October), before and after the convention.
* 2001: Broadcast 99 (5 October), [[Warren Holland]] on the cancellation of DecipherCon.
* 2002: Broadcast 116 (22 February), announcing the dates of DecipherCon 2002.
* 2003: Broadcasts 156, 170 and 171, on DecipherCon's move to Gen Con and the World Championships held there.

The Wayback Machine's copies of Broadcasts 26, 27, 37 and 38 stop at 8 minutes 44 seconds.<ref name="rfd26w">[http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/audio/rfd_99_09_27.ra Radio Free Decipher, Broadcast 26 (27 September 1999)], [[Carol Wisely]] with [[Kendrick Summers]], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000903024602/http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/audio/rfd_99_09_27.ra Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="rfd27w">[http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/audio/rfd_99_10_08.ra Radio Free Decipher, Broadcast 27 (8 October 1999)], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000903024542/http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/audio/rfd_99_10_08.ra Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="rfd37w">[http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/audio/rfd_00_06_09.ra Radio Free Decipher, Broadcast 37 (9 June 2000)], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000903024158/http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/audio/rfd_00_06_16.ra Internet Archive]</ref> Broadcast 171 survives whole.<ref name="rfd171w">[http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/audio/rfd_03_08_01.ra Radio Free Decipher, Broadcast 171 (1 August 2003)], [[Kyle Heuer]] and [[Evan Lorentz]], Decipher. == What survives ==

The Internet Archive's Wayback Machine holds copies of pages from all three sites, including photo pages and photos. Its copies of the 1999 audio are the <code>.ram</code> pointer files only.<ref name="ram99" /> The 2000 finals videos survive. In February 2022 the YouTube channel Player's Council posted all three finals:
* the Star Wars CCG final (1:21:09)<ref name="yt-sw">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q0sFxQ2i3Hk DecipherCon 2000 SWCCG World Championship Final Confrontation - Yannick Lapointe vs Matt Sokol], Player's Council (YouTube, 19 February 2022). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008004102/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q0sFxQ2i3Hk Internet Archive]</ref>
* the Star Trek CCG final (47:23)<ref name="yt-st">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QuJ6BgUEXQs DecipherCon 2000 STCCG 1E World Championship Final Confrontation - Brian Sykes vs Eric Johnfauno], Player's Council (YouTube, 18 February 2022). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016010842/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QuJ6BgUEXQs Internet Archive]</ref>
* the Young Jedi final (28:02)<ref name="yt-yj">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=po7x8VJLhlM DecipherCon 2000 Young Jedi World Championship Final Confrontation - Ian Vincent vs Philippe Parise], Player's Council (YouTube, 18 February 2022). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016010935/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=po7x8VJLhlM Internet Archive]</ref>

The Star Wars video opens with the announcer's welcome: "this is the Star Wars CCG World Finals".<ref name="yt-sw" />
